newsitem.title: USA: Wendy's plans building 750-800 stores in '97.
newsitem.headline: Wendy's plans building 750-800 stores in '97.

text.p: Wendy's International Inc said Wednesday it plans to open or begin construction on 750 to 800 new Wendy's and Tim Hortons stores worldwide in 1997.
Gordon Teter, chairman, Wendy's chief executive officer and president of the company disclosed the plan as Wendy's reported record fourth quarter and full year 1996 results.
Teter said the plan includes building about 350 new Wendy's shops in the U.S., 170 in international markets and 270 Tim Hortons.
"We're very pleased with Wendy's growth in the fourth quarter and the full year," Teter said.
Teter said average sales per restaurant grew nearly seven percent in domestic company stores for the quarter, including 10 percent in December.
But he noted that higher food costs and start-up costs for training and implementation of fresh stuffed pitas affected company margins.
As a result, domestic operating margins decreased one-half point from a year ago, to 13.1 percent, he said.
Margins steadily improved during the quarter, and in December they were favorable to the prior year, he said, adding he expects the improving trend to continue in 1997.

Also for 1997, Wendy's expects to finalize an agreement with a new franchisee in Venezuela to convert 32 TropiBurger restaurants into Wendy's, with the first conversion expected this summer, the company said.
* Wendy's franchised 63 company-owned restaurants to new and existing franchisees for an asset gain of about $19 million.

* A record 727 Wendy's and Tim Hortons were opened or under construction. Wendy's opened 343 restaurants, finishing the year with 4,933 restaurants open and 120 under construction. Tim Hortons opened 200 stores and ended the year with 1,384 open and 64 under construction. The Wendy's system totalled 6,317 restaurants worldwide.
* Average sales in standard Wendy's U.S. restaurants reached $1 million for the first time.
For the fourth quarter ended December 29 profits jumped 122 percent to to $40.2 million, or $0.30 a share fully diluted, against $18.2 million, or $0.15 a share a year ago.

Revenues for the latest quarter were $488.8 million, versus $459.4 million and systemwide sales rose 10 percent to $1.39 billion. The 1995 figures include a $22.4 million (pretax) one-time special charge for expenses related to the merger with Tim Hortons, it said.
Net income for the full year was $155.9 million, a 42% increase over the $110.1 million posted a year ago.

Fully diluted earnings per share were $1.19 versus $.88 and revenues were $1.90 billion versus $1.75 billion. Systemwide sales were up 8% to $5.43 billion. In 1995, the company had $49.7 million (pretax) in one-time special charges related to the Hortons merger.
In 1996, the company benefitted from a lowering of merger-related reserve estimates required in the merger with Tim Hortons.
